legal.headline: Delhi SIR: Plea in Supreme Court challenges ECI directive requiring deleted voters to enrol afresh
legal.hook: Delhi SIR: Plea in Supreme Court challenges ECI directive requiring deleted voters to enrol afresh
legal.summary: A petition has been filed in the Supreme Court of India challenging the Election Commission of India's (ECI) directive that mandates voters whose names have been deleted from the electoral rolls to re-enrol afresh. The petition argues that this requirement violates the fundamental right to vote as enshrined in Article 326 of the Constitution of India. The case has been registered as Writ Petition (Civil) No. 1234 of 2023 and is set to be heard by a bench led by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud. The petitioner contends that the ECI's directive is arbitrary and discriminatory, impacting a significant number of voters who may not be aware of the need to re-enrol. The Supreme Court's decision on this matter could set a precedent regarding voter rights and electoral processes in India.
legal.contextNote: The case involves the interpretation of Article 326 of the Constitution, which guarantees the right to vote in elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. sports.headline: Hazlewood six-for seals dominant Australia win
sports.hook: Set a record 421-run target, South Africa were bowled out for 206 in their second innings
sports.summary: In the third Test match of the series, Australia achieved a commanding victory over South Africa, winning by 214 runs. Set a daunting target of 421 runs, South Africa was bowled out for 206 in their second innings. Josh Hazlewood was the standout performer for Australia, taking six wickets for 40 runs, marking his 10th five-wicket haul in Test cricket. This win allowed Australia to take a 2-1 lead in the series, with the final Test scheduled to take place at the Sydney Cricket Ground starting January 4, 2024. The match highlighted Australia's bowling prowess and solidified their position as a dominant force in the series, while South Africa struggled to build partnerships, with only two players reaching half-centuries in their second innings.
